title: Fixed points of nonexpansive maps
description: OpenAI's solution (2026) of Kirk's problem: every nonexpansive self-map of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point, for the given norm. The course reduces to a minimal invariant set where approximate fixed points are diametral (Goebel–Karlovitz), finds an anchor point through resolvents and an idempotent in a compact semigroup of maps (Ellis), builds an infinite tree of maps whose functionals are chosen against compact families of predicted outputs, and switches its leaves to a common approximate fixed point to obtain a contradiction.

units.title: Minimal invariant sets and diametral sequences

prerequisites: foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hahn-banach-baire-and-the-basic-theorems-on-banach-spaces (Theorem 1.1 Zorn; Corollary 2.3 Hahn-Banach; Theorem 4.2 uniform boundedness; Theorem 6.3 strict separation); lesson weak-topologies-tychonoff-banach-alaoglu-mazur-bipolars-krein-milman-and-eberlein-smulian (Theorem 2.3 Tychonoff; Theorem 3.1 Banach-Alaoglu; Theorem 4.1 Mazur)
tingleys-problem lesson ultrapowers-and-darbos-fixed-point-theorem (Lemma 1.1, free ultrafilters on N)
